supporting_observations.claim: At 13:43:04 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01, attributed to BLUEFIN\mia.santos in the proxy log, fetched the file raw.githubusercontent.com/bluefin-it/tools/main/u.ps1 and received HTTP 200.
The script fetch occurred shortly after the reported PowerShell window around 13:40 UTC, so it may be related to the alert; the available records do not show that the script was executed.

The observed download is not the documented workstation-patching method: inventory context says IT runs the patch script from WS-KITO-01 using a FILE-BLU-01 share, whereas this record shows a script fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com by mia.santos's workstation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status information reports a winsec and Sysmon logging outage on WS-MSANTOS-01 from 13:25 to 14:15 UTC, covering the reported PowerShell activity and the script fetch. Endpoint process creation, command-line, and related events for that interval therefore are not available in the supplied evidence.
The proxy record establishes a successful HTTP fetch, but the supplied evidence does not include the script contents, hash, or execution telemetry.
claims_not_established: Whether u.ps1 was executed on WS-MSANTOS-01, by what process or account context, or with what command-line arguments.
Whether the fetched script is an authorized Bluefin IT tool or has been modified or compromised.
Whether the PowerShell window reported by mia.santos was caused by this script fetch or by another activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain endpoint process and PowerShell telemetry for WS-MSANTOS-01 during 13:25–14:15 UTC, including command lines, script-block or transcription logs, and process ancestry.
Retrieve the exact u.ps1 content and hash for the fetched revision; verify the repository, commit, and file against an independently trusted Bluefin IT source.
Check endpoint forensic artifacts for evidence that the file was saved or executed, and confirm with IT whether this download was authorized.
